findings.reason: Original standalone tiles show the complete algebraic verification but no figure. A concrete two-case projection sketch materially clarifies how the null half-line collapses the nonpositive half of the normal score to the atom at zero. The useful addition is warranted independently of the complete proof.
findings.action: Added a two-row TikZ projection sketch with explanatory Remarks prose. Both signs of G and squared distances are shown; the existing step 5.1 supplies the mixture law.

correction: Appended explanatory prose and a fenced TikZ figure to existing Remarks only. Original file is an exact byte prefix of the repaired file; metadata including status: published is byte-identical.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Full local cone C=R and null cone C_0=(-infinity,0], with limiting scalar score G~N(0,1).
diagram_math_checks.justification: Verification step 4.1 explicitly identifies these cones and I=1; both h axes therefore represent the same real local model. The thick left half-axis denotes C_0, with endpoint 0 included.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Projection pi_C0:R -> C_0 sends G to min(G,0).
diagram_math_checks.justification: Step 4.1 gives full and null local maximizers Z_n and min(0,Z_n). Euclidean projection on this closed half-line is G itself for G<=0 and 0 for G>0, as depicted on the two axes.

diagram_math_checks.relation: d(G,C_0)^2=0 for G<=0, and d(G,C_0)^2=G^2 for G>0.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Since I=1 and C=R, the distance from G to the full cone is zero. The bottom double arrow is the positive length G from 0 to the positive score; its square agrees with (G vee 0)^2 in step 5.1. The top point is its own projection.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Each sign case has probability 1/2; the zero-distance case supplies the atom and the positive case supplies the half-weight chi-square-one component.
diagram_math_checks.justification: F1 gives the continuous even standard normal density, so P(G=0)=0 and each half-line has probability 1/2. Step 5.1 derives the resulting mixture explicitly. The caption cites this step rather than asserting an unproved new distribution.
